# derived from monero v0.18.5.1 source, not captured from a run
# Expectation for `settings_valid` against input/config.toml. See
# tests/fixtures/doctor/settings_valid/expect.json for the FMONERO_CONFIG_DIR seam and the
# Settings::invalid_keys() contract.
#
# THIS CASE: THE FILE IS NOT TOML. §7.1's condition is "config.toml PARSES and every key is in the §4
# table"; the base case exercises the second half, this one the first. Verified with a real TOML parser:
# the file fails at the unterminated string on its `network` line, and there are two more errors after it
# (`prune = maybe`, and a `[wallet` header with no closing bracket) so a recovering parser still fails.
#
# THE REASON THIS CASE MATTERS MORE THAN AN INVALID VALUE: Context::load() reads config.toml, and EVERY
# command goes through Context::load(). If an unparsable file makes the loader return Err, then the one
# command whose job is to repair it -- `fmonero doctor --fix` -- is the one command the breakage locks
# out, and the user's only route back is to delete the file by hand, which no --help text tells them. So
# the loader must degrade to defaults and let THIS CHECK report the file it could not read. That is a
# statement about Context::load, not about the doctor, and nothing else in DESIGN.md §7.1 forces it --
# which is why the case is fixtured rather than left to a unit test on Settings.
# SECOND-ORDER CONSEQUENCE, worth stating because it is easy to get wrong: with the file unparsable,
# `Settings` in memory holds DEFAULTS, so every other check in the run sees default settings rather than
# the user's. The detail must therefore make clear that the whole document was unreadable -- not that
# some key was wrong -- or the reader will trust the neighbouring rows more than they should.
# status `warn`, severity `warn`, class A, `fixable` true, from §7.1's row -- the same as the base case,
# because the remedy is the same: WriteFile{config_file(), Settings::to_toml_bytes(&repaired), 0o600}
# through mutate, with the verbatim backup and sha256 pair that let `doctor undo latest` hand these exact
# broken bytes back (§7). Here `repaired` is the WHOLE default document, since nothing in the file is
# recoverable; in the base case only the four bad keys are rewritten.
# THAT UNDO IS THE POINT OF THE BACKUP: a user whose hand-edited config the doctor overwrote can get
# their text back and find the typo, instead of being told their settings were reset.
